patterns.usage_note: Formal, letter-and-greeting Japanese for an occasion framed as a welcome opportunity, so it fits 帰国の折に or お立ち寄りの折に and sits badly on unwelcome events such as accidents, though adverse ongoing states are fine (お忙しい折に, ご多忙の折); bare commands and prohibitions are rare after it, though polite requests in ください and お願いします are routine. It attaches to a dictionary- or た-form verb, an i-adjective, or N+の. Sibling 際に is the neutral procedural 'when you do X', while 折 keeps the flavour of 'should the chance come'; 折の is the adnominal shape and 折にゃ the contracted colloquial one.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]の家[いえ]を訪[おとず]れた折[おり]に、古[ふる]い写真[しゃしん]を見[み]つけた。
examples.english: When I paid my grandfather's house a visit, I came across some old photographs.

examples.ruby: ご帰国[きこく]の折[おり]に、ぜひご連絡[れんらく]ください。
examples.english: Do get in touch when you're back in the country.

examples.ruby: 来春[らいしゅん]そちらへ伺[うかが]う折[おり]に、お目[め]にかかれれば幸[さいわ]いです。
examples.english: I would be delighted to see you when I come your way next spring.

patterns.usage_note: Literary and epistolary: 折柄 (折 + the suffix 柄 'given the nature or circumstances of') presents the prevailing season or conditions as the backdrop for the concern or event that follows, which is why it is a fixture of seasonal greetings — 寒さ厳しい折から、ご自愛ください. Its adnominal shape 折からの modifies a following noun with the sense 'the ~ that happened to be falling/blowing at the time' (折からの雨). Where sibling 折に points at a chance to do something, 折から points at circumstances you are living through, and in the greeting formulas that dominate its use it is overwhelmingly non-past (寒さ厳しい折から), not た-form.

examples.ruby: 梅雨[つゆ]の折[おり]から、どうぞご自愛[じあい]ください。
examples.english: With the rainy season upon us, please do take care of yourself.

examples.ruby: 寒[さむ]さ厳[きび]しい折[おり]から、皆様[みなさま]のご健康[けんこう]をお祈[いの]りします。
examples.english: In this season of bitter cold, I wish you all continued good health.

examples.ruby: 折[おり]からの雨[あめ]で運動会[うんどうかい]は取[と]りやめになった。
examples.english: The rain that had set in just then got sports day called off.

patterns.usage_note: The neutral formal 'when' of announcements, manuals, forms and business speech; it is indifferent to whether the occasion is welcome or not, so unlike sibling 折に it is at home in warnings, prohibitions and unwelcome events (事故の際に, 故障した際には); both take polite requests freely. It attaches to a dictionary- or た-form verb or to N+の, and it prefers occasions worth singling out, so it sounds starched on everyday trivia where 時 would do (歯[は]を磨[みが]く時 rather than 磨く際). 際には is the topicalized form, and には contracts to にゃ in casual speech, though 際にゃ itself is rare.

examples.ruby: 機械[きかい]を使用[しよう]する際[さい]に、必[かなら]ず手袋[てぶくろ]をつけてください。
examples.english: When operating the machine, be sure to put on gloves.

examples.ruby: 口座[こうざ]を開[ひら]いた際[さい]に、印鑑[いんかん]の登録[とうろく]も済[す]ませた。
examples.english: When I opened the account, I got the seal registration out of the way too.

examples.ruby: 面接[めんせつ]の際[さい]に、志望[しぼう]動機[どうき]を詳[くわ]しく聞[き]かれた。
examples.english: At the interview they questioned me closely about why I wanted the job.
